recognize_zh: 細胞離心抹片上只有四顆異常髓系細胞：右側較大的一顆核分兩葉、細胞質灰藍，可能是小型巨核細胞（micromegakaryocyte），其餘為核形不規則的未成熟細胞；解析度有限，單憑此圖無法確立加速期。
features: Small cluster of four nucleated cells on a sparse cytocentrifuge-like background
Largest cell with a bilobed nucleus and gray-blue, faintly granular cytoplasm, possibly a micromegakaryocyte
Two cells with irregular folded nuclei and pale granular cytoplasm (immature granulocytes)
One smaller cell with dense purple cytoplasm obscuring the nucleus, possibly a basophil
Single red cell; fine granule and chromatin detail limited by resolution
describe_en: The preparation shows a small cluster of four nucleated cells. The largest has a bilobed nucleus and gray-blue, faintly granular cytoplasm, raising the possibility of a micromegakaryocyte, while two cells with irregular folded nuclei resemble immature granulocytes and one smaller cell with dense purple cytoplasm may be a basophil. Chromatin and granule detail are limited at this resolution, and cell lineage cannot be assigned with confidence without immunostaining (e.g., CD61) or a larger field. Such dysplastic megakaryocytes and basophils support, but do not by themselves establish, accelerated phase of CML.

ddx.vs: Monocytic cells have lacy chromatin and vacuolated gray cytoplasm and are NSE/CD14-positive, whereas micromegakaryocytes are CD61/CD42b-positive.
Plasma cells have clock-face chromatin with a perinuclear hof, and blasts have fine chromatin with nucleoli, unlike the dense lobulated megakaryocyte nucleus.
MDS micromegakaryocytes occur without BCR::ABL1 and without the granulocytic hyperplasia and basophilia of CML.
